title: Carbonised Grease vs Fresh Grease
excerpt: Fresh grease is relatively soft and oily; carbonised or heavily heat-aged grease is darker, harder and more strongly bonded because heat, oxidation, polymerization and food solids have changed the deposit.
content_html:
Fresh grease and heavily heat-aged grease behave differently during cleaning. Fresh grease is usually soft, oily and easier to emulsify. Older deposits exposed to heat and air can oxidize, polymerize and combine with food solids until they become dark, hard or resin-like.

Fresh grease

Fresh deposits are dominated by liquid or semi-liquid fats and oils. They usually respond to compatible degreasing chemistry, moderate mechanical action and prompt recovery.

Heat-aged and polymerized grease

Scientific reviews of cooking oils describe oxidation and polymerization during repeated heating. Polymerized material can form sticky brown or resin-like deposits that adhere more strongly to metal surfaces.

What people often call carbonised grease

In kitchen maintenance, “carbonised grease” commonly describes very dark, hardened deposits containing aged grease plus cooked-on or charred food material. It is a practical maintenance term rather than a single pure chemical substance.

Why cleaning demand increases

Hard deposits reduce chemical penetration and may require longer compatible dwell, more mechanical action, repeated cycles or specialist methods. Simply increasing cleaner concentration can damage the surface without fully removing the deposit.

Where hard deposits develop fastest

Fryer surrounds, grills, ovens, hood interiors and exhaust paths receive heat plus grease-laden vapour, so deposits can age faster than on cooler kitchen surfaces.

Comparison

FeatureFresh greaseHeat-aged/carbonised grease
FeelSoft, oily, slickSticky, resin-like or hard
ColourLight to amberBrown to very dark
Bond to surfaceUsually lowerOften stronger
Cleaning demandRoutine degreasing may be enoughMore dwell/action or specialist process may be needed

Prevention is easier than restoration

Frequent removal of thin grease film reduces the time available for heat ageing, oxidation and soil layering. This is one reason routine degreasing and exhaust maintenance should not be delayed.

Practical takeaway

Fresh grease is mainly a removable oily film; heat-aged or carbonised deposits are changed materials. Diagnose the deposit before choosing chemistry, dwell and mechanical action.

  2. PMC — Heated Culinary Oil Oxidation and Polymerization Review.
